enhanced_information: Excitatory postsynaptic potentials (EPSPs) are graded potentials that result from neurotransmitter binding, leading to depolarization of the postsynaptic membrane. They can summate with other EPSPs, contributing to the likelihood of reaching the threshold for action potential generation. EPSPs do not follow an all-or-nothing principle, as they vary in amplitude and can occur repeatedly without a refractory period. While they can spread passively along the membrane, influencing distant parts of the neuron, they are not hyperpolarizing. Therefore, the correct statements regarding EPSPs are that they can be added and they spread long distances.
analysis: Excitatory postsynaptic potentials (EPSPs) are graded potentials that can vary in amplitude and can summate, meaning they can be added together to increase the likelihood of reaching the threshold for action potential generation. They are not all-or-nothing, as that characteristic applies to action potentials. EPSPs are depolarizing rather than hyperpolarizing, and they do not have a refractory period like action potentials do. They can spread over short distances but are not typically associated with long-distance propagation. Therefore, the most accurate statement is that they can be added.
